skill.name: email-systems
skill.description: Design reliable transactional and marketing email systems with queues, authentication, deliverability controls, consent, templates, bounce handling, and monitoring.
skill.summary: Build dependable email infrastructure that reaches inboxes and respects recipient preferences.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 24 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder URLs, or defensive email guidance. A separate high-severity issue remains: the bounce webhook example trusts an unsigned request body, enabling forged suppression events if implemented directly.

remediation.issue: The bounce webhook example accepts provider events without authenticating the sender.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the provider signature against the raw request body before parsing or changing recipient state, and reject stale or replayed events.

content.value_statement: Email systems often fail through weak deliverability, missing consent controls, or unreliable sending. This skill provides patterns for dependable transactional and marketing email infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Design queued transactional email delivery with retries and monitoring.
Separate transactional and marketing traffic to protect deliverability.
Plan SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and IP warm-up practices.
Handle bounces, complaints, unsubscribes, and recipient preferences.
Create accessible multipart email and React Email templates.
Track campaign outcomes and recover from partial send failures.
limitations: It does not configure DNS records, providers, queues, or production infrastructure.
Code examples require adaptation, authentication, validation, and testing before production use.
Legal requirements vary by region and require qualified review.
Provider-specific limits, pricing, APIs, and deliverability policies may change.

use_cases.title: Launch Transactional Email
use_cases.description: Plan reliable password resets, receipts, confirmations, queues, retries, and bounce processing.

use_cases.title: Improve Campaign Deliverability
use_cases.description: Review authentication, consent, list hygiene, warm-up, unsubscribe, and monitoring practices.

use_cases.title: Audit Email Architecture
use_cases.description: Identify reliability, accessibility, compliance, and reputation risks across an existing email system.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Email Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this email flow: [describe flow]. Identify reliability, deliverability, consent, and accessibility gaps. Recommend the three highest-priority improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single transactional or marketing email.

prompt_templates.title: Design Transactional Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a transactional email system for [product]. Include provider separation, queue behavior, retries, idempotency, authenticated webhooks, bounce handling, and monitoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate architecture planning for critical messages.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Marketing Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an email operations plan for [audience and volume]. Cover consent, segmentation, preferences, authentication, warm-up, rate limits, complaints, and success metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced campaign preparation for a permission-based list.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production System
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this email architecture: [details]. Build a prioritized risk register covering security, deliverability, privacy, reliability, recovery, observability, and provider dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cross-functional assessment of an existing system.

output_examples.input: Review our password reset email flow, which sends directly during the web request.
output: Priority: move delivery to a durable queue so provider latency does not block the request.
Add bounded retries, idempotency, expiration monitoring, and delivery alerts.
Authenticate bounce and delivery webhooks before changing recipient state.

output_examples.input: Plan deliverability for a new marketing domain sending 20,000 weekly messages.
output: Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC before the first campaign.
Warm sending volume gradually using recently engaged, consented recipients.
Track hard bounces, complaints, inbox placement, unsubscribes, and provider limits.

output_examples.input: Audit an HTML-only newsletter without an unsubscribe header.
output_examples.output: Add a readable plain-text part, visible one-click unsubscribe, List-Unsubscribe headers, meaningful preview text, and accessible image alternatives.

best_practices: Separate critical transactional messages from marketing traffic and reputation.
Authenticate domains and provider webhooks before processing production email events.
Monitor each send, suppress hard bounces, and honor complaints or unsubscribes immediately.
anti_patterns: Do not send marketing email to purchased, scraped, or unconsented contacts.
Do not send large volumes from a new domain or IP without gradual warm-up.
Do not trust webhook payloads or update recipient state without signature verification.

faq.question: Does this skill send email directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture, implementation patterns, validation checks, and operational guidance.

faq.question: Which email providers does it support?
faq.answer: The guidance is provider-neutral, with examples mentioning services such as Postmark, Resend, SendGrid, ConvertKit, and Customer.io.

faq.question: Does it cover transactional and marketing email?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains their different reliability, consent, reputation, and infrastructure requirements.

faq.question: Can it guarantee inbox placement?
faq.answer: No. Inbox placement depends on authentication, sender reputation, content, recipient engagement, provider policy, and ongoing operations.

faq.question: Does it provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It highlights consent and unsubscribe practices, but regional requirements require qualified legal review.

faq.question: Are the code examples production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Add provider authentication, input validation, error handling, idempotency, privacy controls, and environment-specific tests before production use.
